::: {.why}
The curve you plotted last night contains the holding period, the turnover and most of the capacity, and reading it correctly saves you a parameter sweep.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Read a holding period off an IC decay curve and justify it against the turnover cost it implies.
- Say what a decay curve that peaks at a lag greater than zero would mean, and whether yours does.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Produce decay curves for all four signals with intervals at each horizon, and read off the horizon at which each stops being distinguishable from zero. Then compute the implied turnover for a rule that rebalances at that horizon and the cost it implies from qlib/costs.py.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Find the optimum properly: net information ratio is the product of IC and the square root of breadth, minus cost, and all three vary with horizon. Plot net expected performance against rebalance frequency for one signal and mark the maximum. This is the calculation that replaces a parameter sweep for holding period.
:::
:::
